name: Reference greenhouse
description: The reference scenario: 32 tomato plants in a small three-span house with fans, a heater, a dehumidifier, roof vents, sensors and a camera, from spring into summer, 120 days

notes.scenario: The reference scenario of P09 (reference-greenhouse-v1): modest enough to run on a laptop, complete enough to exercise every subsystem together. The viewer lists it first.
notes.envelope: Three 3.2 m spans, three 4 m bays, 4 m to the gutters: a small Venlo-style roof. A vent near each span's ridge, along the middle of the house, shut until commanded; a door in the front gable, by the path.
notes.layout: Four rows of eight plants along the house, 1.6 m apart about its middle, 0.75 m between plants, on gutters under two crop wires 3.6 m up, 30 cm either side of each row, a high-wire double row whose plants are trained to the wires by turns, with a pipe rail along each row; a path across the front. Its equipment, all off until commanded: two fans high over the front path blowing down the house, a 15 kW heater in the back right corner, and a dehumidifier against the left side wall, halfway along. Its sensors: temperature and humidity at crop height in the front and back halves, the back pair imperfect; an anemometer in the right fan's jet; CO2 in the middle; PAR in the canopy and under the roof; a camera at the front looking down the middle path; and a weather station 3 m in front of the house.
notes.crop_model: Organ by organ (P09.3): each plant a transplant of the plant lab's crop, its traits drawn from the seed, living each day in the house's mean air and its own light. The other scenarios keep the simple daily model.
notes.crop_work: Every week, a harvest round picks every red fruit, so that ripe fruit does not pile up and each plant's history lists what was picked from it; then a lowering round keeps each plant's top 30 cm or more under its wire, laying its bare lower stem down round its row's gutter, as a high-wire crop is lowered.
notes.start_date: 1 March, for 120 days: March's nights need heat, June's days need venting, and the crop bears red fruit for its last month or more.
notes.opening_day: Where the viewer opens it: the run's first day with red fruit, kept beside this manifest as a checkpoint (openings/reference_greenhouse.json.gz), so that its later days carry on from it rather than from the run's start. `python tests/test_opening_day.py --update` writes it again.
notes.random_seed: Seed 42, which the final QA resets to.
notes.climate: A cool, damp March night to start: 14 °C and 80% inside.
notes.weather: The cold spring day (the cold_spring_day preset), every day: a synthetic day does not follow the season, though the sun does.
notes.daily: Its climate by the clock, every day (P09.4): the heater full from 17 h, set back to 80% at 23 h, full again from 5 h before dawn, half at 7 h and off at 9 h; the roof vents half open at 9 h, fully from 11 h, half from 18 h and shut at 20 h; both fans from 8 h to 20 h. A fixed schedule cannot follow the season: from May the morning's heat and an early sun meet before the vents open fully, and the house peaks near 30 °C at 9 h; a climate computer's setpoints would follow it.
